newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cenbank, police probe alleged debt fraud.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cenbank, police probe alleged debt fraud.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank and police were investigating four broking houses and a small bank for suspected participation in an alleged multi-million dollar fraud scheme involving state and municipal bonds, officials said.
Central Bank president Gustavo Loyola was due to hold a news conference in Sao Paulo at 1100 local/1400 GMT to explain the investigations, a bank spokesman said.
Newspapers said Central Bank and tax officials, accompanied by federal police officers, seized Thursday documents from financial institutions suspected of involvement in the scheme.

The investigation springs from a Parliamentary Committee of Inquiry in Brazil's Senate which was set up late last year to look into alleged irregularities involving debt issued by several states and the municipality of Sao Paulo.
Senators involved in the inquiry say they have evidence showing the financial institutions bought bonds at artifically low prices and sold them on immediately at a profit.
The bonds were then successively bought and sold by a chain of other financial insitutions before ending up in public sector pension funds, the senators allege.
They also accuse the issuers of the bonds, including economic powerhouse state Sao Paulo, of misusing the funds raised which, by law, were exclusively for paying court settlements.
